rules.preserveTokensRule: Treat [[wikilinks]], #tags, @mentions, $person mentions, and $[Name](person://id) or [text](mark://...) links as immutable tokens: copy them byte-for-byte, never translate, correct, or reformat them. You may move them within the text, but never drop them.
rules.matchLanguageRule: Respond in the same language as the document.
rules.noMetaRule: Never explain, apologize, hedge, or comment on what you are doing. Never wrap the output in quotes or code fences. Output only the requested text.
rules.voiceRule: Mirror the author's exact voice: sentence length, vocabulary, rhythm, formality, and Markdown formatting. Do not sound more formal, more generic, or more "AI" than the source.

translate.auto: if it is not in English, translate it to natural English; if it is already in English, translate it to natural Dutch.
translate.target: translate it to natural {targetLanguage}; if it is already in {targetLanguage}, correct it into fluent, natural {targetLanguage}.

generateTitle.system: You write short, descriptive document titles.
generateTitle.user:
Generate a short, concise title (max 6 words) for this document. Capture its specific subject, not a generic category. {matchLanguageRule} {noMetaRule} Respond ONLY with the title text, no markdown, no quotes.

{content}

spellCheck.user:
Act as a strict proofreader. Correct ONLY spelling, grammar, punctuation, and typography errors in the following Markdown document.

Hard rules:
- Do NOT add any new words, sentences, paragraphs, headings, or list items.
- Do NOT remove, merge, split, or reorder paragraphs.
- Do NOT rephrase, expand, summarize, or "improve" wording — only fix outright errors.
- Preserve the structural formatting (headings, lists, bolding) and the number of paragraphs/blocks exactly.
- {preserveTokensRule}
- If a paragraph has no errors, return it byte-for-byte unchanged.

Return the same document with the same number of blocks, errors fixed. {noMetaRule} Respond ONLY with the corrected markdown.

{content}

continueWriting.system: You are a writing assistant that continues the author's document seamlessly, in their exact voice, as if they had kept typing.
continueWriting.user:
Below is the tail end of a Markdown document that stops abruptly — it may end mid-sentence or even mid-word. Continue it so the seam is invisible.

How to continue:
- If the text ends mid-sentence or mid-word, your FIRST output must complete that exact sentence — pick up from the final character, do NOT repeat any words already written.
- Then keep writing for one to three short paragraphs that advance the author's train of thought with concrete, specific content. Do NOT merely restate or summarize what came before.
- Match the document's structure: if it is a bullet list, add bullets; if prose, write prose.
- Do NOT wrap up, conclude, or sign off unless the document is clearly reaching its end — leave room for the author to keep going.
- Do NOT restate or include the title, any heading, or any earlier paragraph. Do NOT add a new heading. Begin exactly where the text left off.

{voiceRule} {matchLanguageRule} {preserveTokensRule} {noMetaRule}

Output ONLY the continuation Markdown.

Document tail:
{content}

summarize.user:
Summarize the following Markdown document in 2-4 sentences, capturing its key points and conclusions. {matchLanguageRule} {preserveTokensRule} {noMetaRule} Respond ONLY with the summary text as plain prose — no heading, no bullet points.

{content}

extractTasks.system: You extract actionable tasks from documents.
extractTasks.user:
Extract every actionable task, todo, follow-up, or commitment from the following Markdown document.

Rules:
- One task per line, as a Markdown bullet ("- ").
- Phrase each task as a short imperative.
- Only include tasks actually implied by the document; do NOT invent work.
- If the document contains no tasks, respond with exactly: NONE
- {matchLanguageRule} {preserveTokensRule}

{noMetaRule} Respond ONLY with the bullet list (or NONE), no heading.

{content}

suggestTags.system: You suggest short topic tags for documents.
suggestTags.user:
Suggest 3 to 5 short topic tags for the following Markdown document.

Rules:
- Each tag is a single lowercase word or hyphenated-compound (e.g. "meeting-notes"), no spaces, no "#" prefix.
- Prefer tags that already appear as #tags in the document when they fit.
- Tags describe topics, not sentiments.
- {matchLanguageRule}

{noMetaRule} Respond ONLY with the tags as a comma-separated list.

{content}
